reviews.comment: Great Prof, worth attending class. He is so passionate, clearly knows the content and teaches it well. Also funny. Occasional attendance quizzes for extra credit and some other extra credit opportunities sprinkled in. Exams very heavily based on lecture notes. Homework is very do-able and based on lecture notes. Allows formula sheet for exams.

Grasley is pretty good. Grader is generous with partial credit IF YOU WRITE EVERYTHING DOWN. I got docked 35% on a quiz once for not specifying the obvious initial values (y(0)0 and y'(0)0) that gave me the CORRECT constants of integration. I literally did it correctly and only got 65 on the quiz. Not Grasley's fault though. He was aight.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Maybe the best prof that I've had in CVEN so far. Really great lecturer that is good at keeping you engaged and helps make a lot of the difficult concepts more understandable. Posts the partial lecture slides online before class, but you'll still need to take some notes during lecture. Only 2 tests which cover a lot of material, but aren't too bad.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great Professor! Makes the driest parts of Eng112 interesting simply because he's a great speaker, loves teaching, and cares whether his students master the material. He'll make you work for your grade, but the homework load is very light. The class  mainly project based with a pellet sorter and Matlab. Be ready for an earful about concrete!

Grasley's Materials Engineering class drew heavily from real-life examples and his own work experience; he was very approachable and always tried to keep things interesting. I definitely see myself remembering many of his lessons in my future career. Exams followed lecture material pretty closely.

Weekly quizzes worth 60% of your grade (one problem, sometimes from the book, Hard AF). Teaches mostly theoretical, not many examples. HW takes a while but if you have Chegg it helps. can't use formula sheets on quizzes like other profs do.
